text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: The cost of x is y dollars.
CheaperThan(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y dollars.
ProvidesFinancialAid(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to y.
Applicant(x) ::: x is a GRE applicant.
ProveEconomicHardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
HasFewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available.
ApplyingToTakeGRE(x) ::: x is applying to take the GRE test.
Premises:
Cost(GRETest, 205) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test.
Cost(GRETest, 205) ∧ CheaperThan(205, 300) ::: $205 is cheaper than $300.
∀x (Applicant(x) ∧ ProveEconomicHardship(x) → ProvidesFinancialAid(ETS, x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x ((LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ∨ HasFewResources(x)) → ProveEconomicHardship(x)) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(Tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
HasFewResources(Tom) ::: Tom has few resources available to him.
ApplyingToTakeGRE(Tom) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
CheaperThan(Cost(GRETest), 300) ::: It costs below US $300 to take the GRE test.
